text: Which voltage-gated ion channels expressed in every brain region have no detectable mRNA in liver and none in kidney, are at the plasma membrane, and are not targets of approved small-molecule drugs?
plan: Protein class: Voltage-gated ion channels AND Brain region category (RNA): any / Detected in all AND Tissue category (RNA): Liver / Not detected AND Tissue category (RNA): Kidney / Not detected AND Subcellular location (ICC): Plasma membrane AND NOT Protein class: FDA approved drug targets / Small molecule drugs
understanding: The query searches for genes categorized as voltage-gated ion channels, with RNA expression across all brain regions, no detectable RNA expression in liver and kidney, localized to the plasma membrane, and excluding targets of approved small-molecule drugs.

trail.why: Selecting the class 'Voltage-gated ion channels' directly matches the requirement without restricting to any specific subclass.

The category 'Detected in all' defines genes detected in every brain region of the dataset, and leaving Level 1 unspecified applies this across the whole dataset without restricting to a specific region.
Selecting 'liver' at Level 1 combined with 'Not detected' at Level 2 identifies genes with mRNA levels below the detection threshold in liver tissue.
The requirement specifies no detectable mRNA in the kidney, which corresponds to selecting 'kidney' at level 1 and 'Not detected' (mRNA below the 1 nTPM detection cut-off) at level 2.
The requirement specifies proteins located at the plasma membrane, so 'Plasma membrane' is selected at Level 1 without restricting reliability or location subcategories at Level 2.

trail.requirement: are not targets of approved small-molecule drugs
trail.why: The filter targets approved small-molecule drug targets under the 'FDA approved drug targets' class to exclude them from the results.

requirements.why: Identifies the functional gene family using the 'Voltage-gated ion channels' class/subclass option.
Filters RNA expression distribution across human brain regions (e.g., expressed in all).
Tissue category (RNA) captures RNA specificity and distribution per human tissue, allowing filtering for genes not detected in liver.
Tissue category (RNA) allows filtering for genes not detected at the RNA level in kidney.
Specifies subcellular localization to the 'Plasma membrane' via immunofluorescence.

requirements.requirement: are not targets of approved small-molecule drugs
requirements.why: Negates the 'Small molecule drugs' category within the drug target protein classes to exclude approved small-molecule targets.
